_howToPublishANewCompanionBuild: THIS FILE IS THE ONLY PLACE YOU EDIT. Three steps, no hand-computed hashes:
1. Upload the new ZIP to  downloads/nerve/<version>-<channel>/  on GitHub.
Use a NEW folder every time. Never replace a file at a path already published.
2. In this file, set: version, channel, releaseDate, and companion.path.
On every deploy `npm run build` reads the actual ZIP and fills in the rest itself:
the SHA-256, the exact byte size, the human-readable size, the download URL and the
filename, then writes the matching .sha256 sidecar next to the ZIP. Because the hash
is computed from the very bytes being served, the published checksum can never drift
The build REFUSES to publish and fails loudly if: the ZIP named in companion.path is
missing, the version string does not appear in the filename, or a status is set to
'available' without the things that status requires. A failed build leaves the
previous deployment serving, so a mistake here cannot break the live site.
A download or Forge link is rendered as a real, clickable control ONLY when its
status is 'available' and its target actually exists. Otherwise it renders as a
non-clickable disabled control. Set a status back to 'pending' to unpublish;

_comment: Set formEnabled to true ONLY after RESEND_API_KEY, FEEDBACK_TO and FEEDBACK_FROM
are set in the Vercel project's environment variables. While it is false the
feedback page hides the form entirely and presents the email route instead, so no
tester fills in a long form only to be told the endpoint is off.
